nodes.title: Google BigQuery: Key Ideas
nodes.content: BigQuery is GCP's serverless data warehouse — petabyte-scale SQL with no clusters to manage. You pay for storage and for bytes scanned by each query (or for slots if you reserve capacity). The exam tests partitioning, clustering, cost control, and access patterns.

flashcards.front: What's the difference between partitioning and clustering?
flashcards.back: Partitioning splits a table into separate physical chunks by date or integer range — queries that filter on the partition column scan only relevant chunks. Clustering sorts data inside each partition by up to 4 columns — further reduces bytes read. Use both: partition by ingest_date, cluster by user_id.

flashcards.front: On-demand vs flat-rate pricing — pick one.
flashcards.back: On-demand: $5/TB scanned, perfect for unpredictable workloads. Flat-rate: reserve N slots (compute units) for $/month or $/year, no per-query cost — pick when you have a steady high query volume and want predictable bills. Most teams start on-demand and switch to flat-rate around ~$10k/month.

flashcards.front: Why does column selection matter so much?
flashcards.back: BigQuery is columnar — `SELECT *` scans every column for every row. `SELECT user_id, ts` scans only those two. On a 10-column table, that's a 5x cost reduction with one keystroke. Never `SELECT *` in production analytics; always project explicitly.

flashcards.front: Where do you put data BigQuery can query directly?
flashcards.back: Native BigQuery storage (best perf, replicated automatically), or external tables over Cloud Storage / Bigtable / Cloud SQL (federated queries, no copy needed but slower and cost-variable). Use native for analytics queries; use external when source-of-truth lives elsewhere.

pairs.stem: A financial company needs to train a regression model to predict loan default probability using 50 structured features stored in BigQuery. The data science team has limited ML engineering experience and wants to avoid writing model training code. Which GCP approach minimizes custom code?
pairs.option: Use BigQuery ML with CREATE MODEL and model_type='LOGISTIC_REG' directly on the BigQuery table

pairs.stem: A healthcare company needs to load 10 years of patient visit records stored as Avro files in Cloud Storage into BigQuery for long-term analytics. The data is static and never changes after loading. Which loading method best balances speed, cost, and simplicity?
pairs.option: Use BigQuery load jobs with WRITE_TRUNCATE to batch-load all Avro files directly from Cloud Storage

pairs.stem: A company stores 50 TB of Parquet files in Cloud Storage. They want data analysts to query these files using SQL without loading them into BigQuery or converting the format. Queries should support joins with BigQuery native tables. Which BigQuery feature enables this?
pairs.option: Use BigQuery Omni to run queries on Cloud Storage Parquet files from the AWS or Azure BigQuery deployments

pairs.stem: A company stores 10 years of financial transaction data in BigQuery. The compliance team needs to run point-in-time queries — seeing the state of the table exactly as it was 45 days ago — without maintaining manual snapshots. Which BigQuery feature enables this?
pairs.option: Enable BigQuery streaming inserts with a deduplicated staging table and replay events up to the target date

pairs.stem: A retail company tracks billions of product view events per day. Analysts need to query the last 7 days of events by product category with sub-second latency. Which BigQuery feature best accelerates these repetitive aggregation queries without moving data?
pairs.option: Partition the table by ingestion time and cluster by category, then run standard SQL queries

pairs.stem: A BigQuery table named `events` is partitioned by `event_date` and has 3 years of data (1,000+ partitions). Most queries filter by a specific `user_id`. Analysts report that queries are still scanning the full table despite date filters. What additional optimization should be applied?
pairs.option: Enable BigQuery table clustering on the `user_id` column so data blocks within each partition are sorted by user_id

nodes.title: Dataflow: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Dataflow. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A streaming pipeline built on Dataflow ingests IoT sensor readings from 10,000 devices. Some devices occasionally go silent for up to 90 seconds before resuming. The team needs to emit one aggregate per device per activity burst, regardless of silence gaps. Which windowing strategy should they use?
flashcards.back: Session windows group events separated by gaps smaller than a defined timeout. With a 90-second gap timeout keyed per device, each continuous burst of sensor data forms one session, and silence for 90+ seconds closes the window. Fixed/tumbling windows split bursts artificially at clock boundaries. Sliding windows create overlapping aggregates. Global windows with periodic triggers do not adapt to per-device activity patterns.

flashcards.front: An e-commerce company's Dataflow streaming pipeline processes order events from Pub/Sub. During flash sales, message volume spikes 20x. The pipeline's workers fall behind and event processing latency climbs to 30 minutes. What should the team configure to automatically handle these spikes without manual intervention?
flashcards.back: Dataflow supports horizontal autoscaling by adding workers up to maxNumWorkers. Raising this ceiling allows the pipeline to scale out during flash-sale spikes and handle 20x volume without manual changes. Switching to batch loses real-time processing. Dead-letter topics handle undeliverable messages, not throughput lag. Message ordering keys serialize delivery per key, which would worsen throughput under spike conditions.

flashcards.front: A startup ingests clickstream events into Pub/Sub and processes them with a Dataflow pipeline that writes to BigQuery. On some days, source systems publish events with timestamps up to 2 hours late due to mobile app offline buffering. The team needs accurate hourly aggregates that account for these late arrivals. What is the correct Dataflow configuration?
flashcards.back: Apache Beam / Dataflow supports allowed lateness on event-time windows. Setting allowed lateness to 2 hours means the window will continue to accept late elements arriving up to 2 hours after the watermark passes the window end. Combined with an accumulating (or accumulating+retracting) trigger, the pipeline emits updated aggregates as late data arrives. Processing-time windows lose event-time accuracy. Re-reading a Pub/Sub topic after window close is not a reliable pattern. BigQuery UPDATE-based correction is complex and expensive.

flashcards.front: A telecom company needs to detect anomalous call patterns in real time. Their Dataflow pipeline uses a 5-minute fixed window over call events. Some legitimate calls last longer than 5 minutes and their end event arrives in the next window. The aggregation must count completed calls per window accurately. What Beam feature handles this?
flashcards.back: Allowed lateness in Apache Beam permits elements whose event timestamp falls in an already-closed window to be assigned to that window and update the result. For a call that started in window W but whose end event arrives after the watermark passes the end of W, allowed lateness (e.g., 10 minutes) ensures it updates window W rather than being discarded. Global windows with count triggers ignore event-time semantics entirely. Sliding windows create overlapping aggregates, double-counting calls. Side inputs provide lookup enrichment, not late-data handling.

pairs.stem: A Dataflow pipeline reads from a Pub/Sub subscription and joins each event with a slowly changing reference dataset (product catalog) that is updated once per day. The reference dataset is 500 MB. What is the most memory-efficient Beam pattern for this enrichment?
pairs.option: Load the reference dataset as a Beam side input (as a Map) and access it inside the main event DoFn

pairs.stem: A startup ingests clickstream events into Pub/Sub and processes them with a Dataflow pipeline that writes to BigQuery. On some days, source systems publish events with timestamps up to 2 hours late due to mobile app offline buffering. The team needs accurate hourly aggregates that account for these late arrivals. What is the correct Dataflow configuration?
pairs.option: Configure Pub/Sub message retention to 2 hours and re-read the topic after each window closes

pairs.stem: A data engineer needs to build a pipeline that reads raw user events from Cloud Storage, applies cleaning transformations (null removal, type casting, deduplication), and loads the results into BigQuery on a daily schedule. The pipeline should run without managing servers and support Python. Which combination is most appropriate?
pairs.option: Use Cloud Functions to read each file from Cloud Storage, transform in-memory, and stream results to BigQuery via the Streaming API

pairs.stem: A streaming pipeline built on Dataflow ingests IoT sensor readings from 10,000 devices. Some devices occasionally go silent for up to 90 seconds before resuming. The team needs to emit one aggregate per device per activity burst, regardless of silence gaps. Which windowing strategy should they use?
pairs.option: Session windows with a 90-second inactivity gap timeout per device key

pairs.stem: An e-commerce company's Dataflow streaming pipeline processes order events from Pub/Sub. During flash sales, message volume spikes 20x. The pipeline's workers fall behind and event processing latency climbs to 30 minutes. What should the team configure to automatically handle these spikes without manual intervention?
pairs.option: Increase the maxNumWorkers setting in the Dataflow pipeline so autoscaling can add workers during spikes

pairs.stem: A Dataflow streaming pipeline processes payment transactions and emits fraud alerts. The fraud detection logic requires looking up each transaction's merchant category code (MCC) from a 10 MB static lookup table stored in Cloud Storage. The lookup must be available on every worker without a network call per element. What is the correct implementation?
pairs.option: Add the MCC CSV file to the Dataflow worker disk via a startup script and read it from the local filesystem in the DoFn

nodes.title: Vertex Ai: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Vertex Ai. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A machine learning team needs to share engineered features — such as user purchase history embeddings — across multiple models in production. Features must be served with low latency for online inference and must be consistent between training and serving. Which GCP service is designed for this use case?
flashcards.back: Vertex AI Feature Store is designed to solve the training-serving skew problem by providing a single source of truth for features used in both model training and online serving. It stores feature values, provides low-latency online serving via the Feature Store API, and supports batch serving for training data consistency. BigQuery queries during inference add latency unsuitable for online predictions. Cloud Storage Parquet files are batch-oriented and cannot serve point lookups with millisecond latency. Pub/Sub is a messaging system, not a feature store. and serve features online via the Feature Store API

flashcards.front: A fraud detection model deployed on Vertex AI Prediction needs to be retrained weekly with fresh transaction data. The retraining pipeline includes data validation, feature engineering, training, evaluation, and conditional deployment. Which GCP service is best suited to automate this recurring ML pipeline?
flashcards.back: Vertex AI Pipelines (built on KFP) is the recommended MLOps orchestration service on GCP. Each step (data validation, feature engineering, training, evaluation, deployment) is a pipeline component, and conditional logic controls deployment based on evaluation metrics. The pipeline is registered in Vertex AI and can be triggered on a schedule via Cloud Scheduler. Cloud Functions chained by Cloud Scheduler lack conditional branching and pipeline artifact tracking. Cloud Composer is a general workflow orchestrator — valid but less integrated with Vertex AI than Vertex AI Pipelines. BigQuery scheduled queries are for SQL transformations, not ML pipeline orchestration.

flashcards.front: A data science team trains a TensorFlow model on Vertex AI custom training. After training, they want to track model versions, compare evaluation metrics across runs, and promote the best version to production. Which Vertex AI feature manages this workflow?
flashcards.back: Vertex AI Experiments records metrics, parameters, and artifacts for each training run, enabling side-by-side comparison. Vertex AI Model Registry stores model versions with lineage, evaluation metadata, and deployment history. Together they provide a complete MLOps versioning and promotion workflow. Cloud Storage object versioning stores files but provides no metrics comparison or deployment integration. Artifact Registry Docker tags track container versions, not ML model evaluation metrics. A BigQuery metrics table is a custom solution that does not integrate with Vertex AI's deployment pipeline.

flashcards.front: A retail company wants to predict customer churn using 20 features from BigQuery. The team wants an AutoML model that automatically selects the best algorithm, handles feature preprocessing, and performs hyperparameter tuning without writing ML code. Which service provides this?
flashcards.back: Vertex AI AutoML Tabular accepts a BigQuery table as input and automatically handles feature preprocessing, algorithm selection (neural architecture search, gradient boosted trees, etc.), and hyperparameter tuning to find the best model. Results include feature importance and evaluation metrics. BigQuery ML AUTOML_CLASSIFIER is a valid option that also runs AutoML from SQL, but Vertex AI AutoML provides more advanced tuning and a richer evaluation UI. Vertex AI Workbench with TPOT requires writing Python code. A hyperparameter tuning job requires a custom training script.

pairs.stem: A fraud detection model deployed on Vertex AI Prediction needs to be retrained weekly with fresh transaction data. The retraining pipeline includes data validation, feature engineering, training, evaluation, and conditional deployment. Which GCP service is best suited to automate this recurring ML pipeline?
pairs.option: Define the pipeline as a Vertex AI Pipeline using KFP (Kubeflow Pipelines) SDK and schedule it with Cloud Scheduler

pairs.stem: A data science team trains a TensorFlow model on Vertex AI custom training. After training, they want to track model versions, compare evaluation metrics across runs, and promote the best version to production. Which Vertex AI feature manages this workflow?
pairs.option: Tag Docker images in Artifact Registry with semantic version numbers and deploy them directly via Cloud Run

pairs.stem: A data team is building a Vertex AI ML pipeline that trains a model on Vertex AI Training, evaluates it, and conditionally deploys it to a Vertex AI Endpoint only if the evaluation AUC exceeds 0.85. Which Vertex AI Pipelines component pattern implements the conditional deployment?
pairs.option: Write a custom Python script that calls the Vertex AI REST API to check AUC and conditionally deploy, triggered by Cloud Scheduler

pairs.stem: A retail company wants to predict customer churn using 20 features from BigQuery. The team wants an AutoML model that automatically selects the best algorithm, handles feature preprocessing, and performs hyperparameter tuning without writing ML code. Which service provides this?
pairs.option: Train a Vertex AI AutoML Tabular model on the BigQuery dataset, letting AutoML handle feature engineering and algorithm selection

pairs.stem: A machine learning team needs to share engineered features — such as user purchase history embeddings — across multiple models in production. Features must be served with low latency for online inference and must be consistent between training and serving. Which GCP service is designed for this use case?
pairs.option: Use Vertex AI Feature Store to define feature groups, ingest batch values,.

pairs.stem: A retail company wants to train a product recommendation model. Training data contains user purchase histories stored in BigQuery. The team needs feature vectors for each user to be consistent across training and serving, and the features must be updated daily with new purchase data. Which architecture best solves the training-serving skew problem?
pairs.option: Train the model on BigQuery data exports and serve predictions using a Vertex AI endpoint that queries BigQuery at inference time

pairs.stem: A machine learning team stores 1,000 feature vectors per user in Bigtable for real-time model inference. Each vector is a float array of 128 dimensions. Reads must complete in under 5 ms. The team is experiencing slow reads during peak hours. What is the most direct fix?
pairs.option: Increase Bigtable cluster node count to add throughput and reduce read latency during peak traffic

pairs.stem: A social platform ingests 5 million user activity events per second via Pub/Sub. Multiple downstream systems — analytics, fraud detection, and personalization — each need to consume every event independently at their own pace. What Pub/Sub architecture supports this requirement?
pairs.option: Create one Pub/Sub topic with a separate subscription for each downstream consumer system

pairs.stem: A data team stores 500 TB of raw JSON log files in Cloud Storage. The data is accessed daily for the first 30 days, then accessed once a month for 6 months, then rarely accessed after that. What lifecycle policy minimizes cost while maintaining data availability?
pairs.option: Set a lifecycle rule to delete all objects after 30 days to eliminate storage costs entirely

pairs.stem: A data engineering team needs to run a short-lived Spark job to process a daily 50 GB CSV file. They want to avoid cluster management, pay only for job duration, and reuse existing PySpark code with minimal changes. Which service best fits this requirement?
pairs.option: Deploy a persistent Dataproc cluster with autoscaling and submit the daily job via Cloud Composer

pairs.stem: A data engineering team runs large Apache Spark ETL jobs on Dataproc. The jobs run once daily for 3 hours and do not require persistent clusters. The team wants to minimize cost. What is the recommended Dataproc pattern?
pairs.option: Create an ephemeral Dataproc cluster at job start, run the Spark job,.

pairs.stem: A company wants to understand which customer data fields in their BigQuery tables contain personally identifiable information (PII) — such as names, email addresses, and national IDs. They need an automated discovery process that scans all tables and classifies sensitive columns. Which GCP service provides this capability?
pairs.option: Apply Vertex AI AutoML NLP to classify each column's values and output a sensitivity label
